# Quick Study Guide: 1.1 Database Context Switching & Creation (use <databaseName>)

> "MongoDB does not have a dedicated command to create a database ahead of time. Switching to a database name that doesn't exist yet (with the use statement) selects it, but the database is only actually created once you insert data into a collection within it. The use statement switches the current database context for all subsequent commands in the session."

## 1. Rapid Visual & Core Concept Summary

At the storage engine boundary, MongoDB decouples logical namespace binding from physical WiredTiger extent allocation. Invoking `use <databaseName>` performs an `O(1)` lexical mutation of the client shell's `db` reference variable in volatile memory without dispatching an allocation RPC to `mongod`.

The architectural state diagram above isolates the volatile client-memory binding of `use schoolDB` from the server-side catalog transaction (`_mdb_catalog.wt`) and `.wt` file allocation triggered by the initial mutating write (`insertOne()`). At the storage engine boundary, this sub-topic governs how `mongod` coordinates `OP_MSG` wire frames, WiredTiger `.wt` table and B-tree index extents, and document-level concurrency latches.

## 2. Must-Know Syntax & Mechanics (Top 75% Exam Focus)

- **L-3.1 Command Syntax (`use <databaseName>`) — Dynamic In-Memory Selection & Active Session Pointer.** In `mongosh`, `use <databaseName>` rebinds the session-scoped `db` proxy object to `<databaseName>` in `O(1)` client time. Every subsequent operation invoked on `db.<collection>` serializes `<databaseName>.<collection>` as the full namespace (`ns`) inside `OP_MSG` wire frames.
- **L-3.2 Execution Behavior — Zero Pre-Allocation & First-Write Disk Materialization.** MongoDB intentionally omits a standalone `CREATE DATABASE` wire command. Until a mutating command (`insert`, `create`, or `update` with `upsert: true`) executes against the namespace, `_mdb_catalog.wt` contains zero entries for `<databaseName>`. Upon the initial write, WiredTiger atomically registers the database namespace, allocates `collection-*.wt`, and initializes the mandatory `_id_` B-tree index (`index-*.wt`).

```javascript
// 1. Volatile client-side lexical binding (Zero server RPC or disk I/O)
use schoolDB
// Internal shell binding: db -> Mongo.getDB("schoolDB")
// At this stage, { listDatabases: 1 } (show dbs) excludes "schoolDB".

// 2. First-write storage engine materialization
db.students.insertOne({ name: "Aditi", age: 18, grade: 8 });
// Server executes OP_MSG { insert: "students", $db: "schoolDB", documents: [...] }
// WiredTiger commits _mdb_catalog.wt entry + collection-*.wt + index-*.wt (_id_).
```

## 3. Rapid Revision Flowchart & Cheat-Sheet Table

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as mongosh Client
    participant WT as mongod (WiredTiger)
    Dev->>Dev: use schoolDB (Rebinds local db pointer in O(1) memory)
    Note over Dev,WT: Zero network RPCs or disk extents allocated
    Dev->>WT: db.students.insertOne({ name: "Aditi", age: 18 })
    WT->>WT: Register schoolDB.students in _mdb_catalog.wt
    WT->>WT: Allocate collection-*.wt & _id_ index-*.wt
    WT-->>Dev: { acknowledged: true, insertedId: ObjectId(...) }
```

| Execution Stage | Shell / Wire Action | `_mdb_catalog.wt` State | WiredTiger `.wt` Files Allocated |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pre-Selection | Default session (`test`) | Unmodified | None |
| `use schoolDB` | Client lexical rebind (`O(1)`) | Zero entries for `schoolDB` | `0` files (volatile pointer only) |
| `insertOne({...})` | `OP_MSG` `{ insert: "students" }` | Registers `schoolDB.students` | `collection-*.wt` + `index-*.wt` (`_id_`) |

## 4. High-Yield Exam Traps

- **Exam Trap — Pre-Write Disconnection**: If a session executes `use schoolDB` and terminates before any write command commits, zero metadata survives on the server.
- **Exam Trap — Case Sensitivity**: Database identifiers in `use <databaseName>` are case-sensitive (`schoolDB` and `schooldb` resolve to distinct namespaces).
- **Exam Trap — Implicit Dual Materialization**: A single `db.students.insertOne(...)` call on a fresh namespace atomically materializes the database, the `students` collection, and the `_id_` B-tree index.
